server.auth_provider.pam_hint_platform: The PAM sign-in works on Linux only, on a server that runs filex directly (not inside Docker, which has no PAM of the host).
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_pamtester_: pamtester is not installed at `{pamtester}`. Install it - Debian/Ubuntu: `sudo apt install pamtester` - Fedora/RHEL: `sudo dnf install pamtester` - then test again.
`{pamtester}` exists but filex cannot run it. Make it executable: `sudo chmod 755 {pamtester}`
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_pam_servic: There is no PAM service file `{pamfile}`. Create it with the two lines `auth required pam_unix.so` and `account required pam_unix.so` (the operating-system accounts page of the docs has variants for sssd and two-factor), then test again.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_sudo_missi: sudo is not installed at `{sudo}`. Install it (`sudo apt install sudo`) or fix sudo_path. Running filex as root instead is not recommended.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_sudo_passw: sudo asks for a password when {runas} runs pamtester. Allow that one command without a password: run `sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/filex` and put in it the line `{runas} ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: {pamtester} {service} *`, then test again.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_sudo_not_a: sudoers does not let {runas} run that command. Run `sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/filex` and put in it the line `{runas} ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: {pamtester} {service} *`, then test again.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_sudo_requi: sudo insists on a terminal (requiretty). In `/etc/sudoers.d/filex` add the line `Defaults:{runas} !requiretty`, then test again. That line is for classic sudo only (`sudo --version` says `Sudo version`): sudo-rs has no such setting, and its `visudo` rejects the line.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_pam_broken: PAM answered with an error or did not answer in time, so it cannot judge sign-ins. Check `/etc/pam.d/{service}` and the system log, and try by hand: `sudo -n {pamtester} {service} nosuchuser authenticate`
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_accepts_an: PAM accepted a user that does not exist with a random password: `{pamfile}` lets everybody in. It must end in a real check such as pam_unix.so or pam_sss.so, never pam_permit.so alone.
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_getent_fai: getent could not be run, so system accounts cannot be told apart. Install it (Debian/Ubuntu: libc-bin, Fedora/RHEL: glibc-common).
server.auth_provider.pam_hint_test_accou: Give the username and password of a real account on this machine to test with. That account becomes a super administrator of filex.
PAM refused that username and password (or the account is locked or expired). Check them by hand: `sudo -n {pamtester} {service} <user> authenticate acct_mgmt`
That is a system or service account (root, a UID below 1000, or a nologin shell). Those never sign in to filex - use a normal account.
That name cannot be a filex username: lowercase letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore; 3 to 32 characters; starting with a letter.
